rationale: The cross-sectional baseline comparison stratified exenatide-trial participants by depression score and compared questionnaire totals. Fresh sage intake and a sage-specific pain response were outside the design.
The HiBalance protocol compares a motor training program with usual care and specifies balance as its primary endpoint. It does not assign dried dates or collect pain as a response to dates.
Early Parkinson participants received deferiprone or vehicle placebo, with MRI iron and drug safety as designated outcomes. Dried dates and food-related pain were outside the treatment comparison.
Participants were followed before and after adding safinamide. The nonmotor and behavioral battery describes medication-associated changes without a dried-date exposure or dried-date pain comparison.
The numerical pain measure refers to subcutaneous apomorphine injection-site nodules. No dried-date exposure was analyzed.

This remote-monitoring protocol recruits Alzheimer disease and behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia patient-caregiver dyads and healthy controls. The design contains no dried-date intervention or pain comparison.

Hospital surveillance compared reported demographics, comorbidities and COVID-19 outcomes. Date refers to a recorded chronological interval. Dried-date consumption and subsequent Parkinson pain were not evaluated.
The assigned exposure was deferiprone, with placebo and two drug doses. Motor UPDRS totals and figure labels do not establish an effect of raw figs on Parkinson rest tremor severity.
The protocol compares wrist-delivered personalized and fixed tactile cues with planned gait measures. Figure references identify devices or procedures. Raw fig intake was outside the design.
The design evaluates trained balance performance and implementation of physiotherapy. It provides no dried-date versus control comparison for Parkinson apathy.
The longitudinal scales can track nonmotor symptoms during add-on safinamide. No group is defined by dried-date intake, so the assessments cannot link that food to apathy.
The study follows continuous subcutaneous apomorphine treatment in advanced Parkinson disease. Its quality-of-life and drug tolerance assessments provide no dried-date apathy comparison.

The apathy monitoring protocol recruits Alzheimer disease and behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia participants. Parkinson disease is background context, with no dried-date assignment or observed food response.

Parkinson status and hospitalization outcomes are analyzed in the SARS-CoV-2 surveillance cohort. Chronological date fields do not represent dried date exposure and the analysis does not test food-related apathy.
The planned endpoints concern cortical activity and aspects of gait or turning under tactile cueing. No dried-date intervention or apathy outcome comparison is specified.

The baseline association uses depression and symptom questionnaires in participants recruited to exenatide trials. Fatigue is an overlapping symptom discussed in interpretation, with no fresh-sage exposure or sage-specific fatigue analysis.
